messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need a concrete set of continuous-batching metrics to feed the Console dashboard and alerts. Primary consumers: runtime, infra, SRE, and product dashboards. Key outputs we want: batch_size distribution, per-request queue_wait_ms, queue_length, worker_pool_saturation, and a saturation indicator per route/model. Who can own the initial schema?

Andre: Infra can own the Prom export and the metrics pipeline (Prom -> Cortex). We should lock low-cardinality labels: route, model_family, region. Avoid model_version by default (cardinality explosion).

Emily: Runtime will emit batch_size histogram and queue_wait_ms histograms. We can also add a per-request header `x-rw-queue-ms` so API and tracing can surface the exact wait time for sampled requests. Proposal metric names: `redwood_batch_size_bucket`, `redwood_queue_wait_ms_bucket`, `redwood_queue_length_gauge`, `redwood_worker_saturation_gauge`.

Li Wei: Agree on names but +1 on cardinality warning. If we need `model_version` for debugging, let's sample 0.5-1% of traffic and send a `redwood_debug_sample{model_version}` counter. Otherwise only `model_family`. Also think twice before adding `route` free text; use a route_id or route_hash to keep cardinality bounded.

Jonathan: From the Console UX side: want to surface distribution (violin or stacked histogram), time-series p50/p95/p99 of queue_wait_ms, and a heatmap for batch_size vs response latency. Alerts: avg queue_wait_ms > 20ms AND worker_saturation > 0.85 for 1m. Also a saturation trend alert if queue_length growing for 5m.

Maya: Rollout plan: instrument in staging, run the existing load tests (50k RPS) and a small microbench that hits extreme tail. After validation, deploy to prod in phases 10%->30%->100% with monitoring gating. Who will provide the gating queries?

Andre: Infra will provide standard queries. Example Prom queries we plan to add to the dashboard: `sum(rate(redwood_queue_length_gauge[1m])) by (route)` and `avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_queue_wait_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))[5m:1m])`. (We should sanity-check that histogram_quantile usage across labels is supported in Cortex.)

Emily: Implementation note: runtime will emit histograms with these labels: `{route_id, model_family, region}` and a `sampled_debug` label only for debug samples. Emitting code example for our Go runtime (promclient):

```
var batchHist = prometheus.NewHistogramVec(prometheus.HistogramOpts{
  Name: "redwood_batch_size",
  Help: "Batch size distribution (per inference)" ,
  Buckets: prometheus.ExponentialBuckets(1, 1.5, 12),
}, []string{"route_id","model_family","region"})

var waitHist = prometheus.NewHistogramVec(prometheus.HistogramOpts{
  Name: "redwood_queue_wait_ms",
  Help: "Time a request spent queued waiting for a batch (ms)",
  Buckets: prometheus.ExponentialBuckets(1, 2, 14),
}, []string{"route_id","model_family","region"})
```

Li Wei: For retention, histograms for every route at 1s resolution could be expensive. We should do 1s ingestion for 1h then rollup to 1m/5m. telemetry-bot — what are current retention/rollup defaults?

telemetry-bot: Current default retention: raw ingest 30d, but high-cardinality histograms are rolled to 5m resolution after 24h. We can add a rollup policy per metric; recommended: keep 1s for 6h, 1m for 30d, then 5m beyond.

Andre: Also: queue_length should be a gauge exported every 10s, not a counter. Worker saturation is derived: `workers_busy / workers_total` as a gauge. We'll add those in the infra exporter.

Maya: Nice. One more: include metrics for continuous batching queue size by priority (e.g., realtime vs batch) — label `priority` with values `realtime|batch`. Keep it low-cardinality.

Emily: We'll add `priority`. Also adding `x-rw-queue-ms` header requires an API contract change — @deploy-bot can we get a PR for spec and SDK bumps?

deploy-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824 — adds `x-rw-queue-ms` header and Prom instrumentation hooks. CI passed on staging.

Jonathan: Once we have initial metrics in staging, I'll wire up the Console prototype (stacked histogram + heatmap) and share screenshots. Can we aim for staging data by end of week?

Maya: End-of-week sounds good. Action items: Andre (infra) — Prom exporters + rollup policy; Emily (runtime) — emit histograms & header; Li Wei (platform) — sample debug path config; Jonathan (product/console) — dashboard prototype; Maya (PM) — coordinate rollout gating and org sign-off.

sre-bot: Note: Please add runbook section `queue_saturation` with steps: 1) check `redwood_worker_saturation_gauge`, 2) fallback to smaller model_family routing, 3) enable autoscale.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll follow up with a short ADR that defines metric names, labels, sampling rates, and rollout plan.

Andre: FYI we might need to bump Cortex ingesters for high histogram cardinality during the 50k RPS load test. I'll schedule a capacity test window.

Emily: Ok will add unit tests for histogram emission and an e2e that asserts header presence for sampled requests.

Jonathan: Thx — ping me once staging has data, I'll start dashboard tiles. :thumbsup:
